rationale: Direct evidence from the primary defining cohort study of intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 77 (Willim et al., 2024) confirms that across the cohort of 33 individuals with heterozygous LRRC7 variants, formal autism spectrum disorder (ASD) was diagnosed in 24% (approximately 8 of 33 individuals). This resolves prior broad categorical/binned descriptions of autistic behaviors or features, confirming that formal clinical ASD criteria are met in approximately one-quarter of affected individuals.

evidence.text: In the primary cohort of 33 individuals harboring heterozygous LRRC7 variants, autism spectrum disorder (ASD) was documented in 24% of cases.

evidence.text: Earlier or secondary reports documented copy number alterations or structural variations in LRRC7 associated with autism-like phenotypes, contributing to wider estimates of autistic traits before primary monogenic single-nucleotide variant cohort sizing.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of LRRC7 variant carriers who do not meet full formal ASD criteria exhibit subthreshold autistic social-communication deficits or repetitive behaviors?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the breakdown between formal DSM-5/ICD ASD diagnosis (24%) versus sub-diagnostic behavioral traits (e.g., stereotypies, social impairment) will refine the behavioral phenotype of LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder.
